A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RLR diffusion-model fine-tuning and Diffusive Chain-of-Thought (DCoT). Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison despite the changed title and extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original image/video generation evaluations, training curves, component ablations, DCoT results and memory measurements in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original image/video and DCoT experiments and reports additional runtime, sampler and sub-chain-length results in Appendices G–I.

M1.justification: The FO/HO/ZO construction and DCoT procedure remain. v3 Section 4.2 adds an explicit budget-based rule for sub-chain length h and prescribes gradient-norm categorical sampling of j instead of v2's uniform sampling. These refine allocation within RLR; the PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun using the revised sampling rule.

E1.justification: Both versions use Pick-a-Pic, HPD v2, ChatGPT-generated video prompts, VBench and the five-prompt hand task. v2 Appendix A.1.1 already describes the full VBench prompt suite; v3's additional metrics and sampler tests do not establish a new dataset or distinct task population.

E2.justification: Main Tables 2–3 retain their comparator sets. The new full-VBench Table 10 includes ModelScopeT2V and Open-Sora while omitting VideoCrafter and DOODL from that expanded comparison; both remain in Table 3. Table 9 also introduces a pure ZO comparator.

E3.justification: v3 adds protocols for timing to a common AES target of 5.4, sweeping h from 0 to 4, and testing a 20-step, order-2 DPM solver. Appendix I adds all 16 VBench metrics and quality/semantic aggregate scoring alongside the retained six-metric comparison. The principal training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test how sub-chain length affects reward, memory and runtime (Table 9), whether RLR works with another sampler (Table 8), and efficiency at a common reward target (Table 7). These substantially extend v2's component ablation, training curves and memory comparison.

E5.justification: The training-curve figures are retained, and v3 introduces no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures. The theoretical variance discussion and parameter-noise scales do not constitute new empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 3 changes RLR subject consistency from 97.53 to 97.64 and its weighted average from 84.61 to 84.63. Table 5 exchanges the complete results assigned to 'without HO' and 'without ZO,' reversing their ranking. Tables 7–10 add substantial timing, sampler, sensitivity and VBench results; main image scores and DCoT scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 introduces formal estimator design spaces, constrained variance minimization and a derived h-selection formula in Appendix J.6. It substantially revises the likelihood-ratio proof using explicit changes of variables and noise-gradient signs, corrects the truncation-bias index from T'-1 to T'+1, and repairs convergence-bound algebra. The stated convergence rate remains unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims of unbiased, low-variance, convergent RLR optimization, stronger image/video alignment and DCoT benefits remain. v3 adds an explicit estimator-design and constrained variance-minimization contribution to the introduction and conclusion; the half-order terminology largely renames the existing hybrid framework.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of diminishing reward gains beyond h=2 relative to increasing memory and runtime, and acknowledges that selecting h is nontrivial. Appendix G also explains the stochastic transitions required for HO when using otherwise deterministic samplers. The established model-collapse and multiscale-generation explanations largely remain.

D1.justification: v3 supplies exact DCoT prompt instructions and examples, selective eta=0.1 noise settings, and additional solver/resource details. Existing hardware, LoRA and principal hyperparameter disclosures remain. The implementation link present in v2's abstract is removed; this establishes a change in access information, not repository availability.

R1.justification: Appendix A expands discussion of DPOK, D3PO, Specialist Diffusion and SPIN, and v3 adds citations including DPM-Solver and Spall's SPSA work. The overall diffusion/alignment/forward-learning positioning remains similar. FLOPS moving from a 2024 preprint citation to its 2025 publication is the same cited work.

P1.justification: v3 extensively reorganizes the narrative around problem formulation, RLR construction, experiments and then theory. Detailed related work and experimental settings move to the appendices, which are reorganized into A–J with a contents page. The introduction, contribution statements, method exposition and conclusion are substantially rewritten.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from two-column to single-column layout, moves the teaser before the abstract, separates the earlier combined method illustration into Figures 2 and 4, and relocates retained plots and tables. New prompt panels and Tables 7–10 substantially expand the displays, while the existing generated-image/video examples and training curves are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens practical evaluation through runtime, sampler and h-sensitivity studies, fuller VBench results and DCoT instructions, while correcting several v2 proof errors. However, its new h-optimality derivation is internally inconsistent: Equation (19) does not give the minimizer of Equation (18)'s quadratic. Unreconciled categorical versus uniform sampling statements and reversed Table 5 rankings with the retained unbiasedness interpretation further obscure the revised method's support. These benefits and scientific inconsistencies prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
